BioSample attribute (treatment: % volumetric water content) + PMID 36135793 / doi:10.1093/plphys/kiac445 - Spatiotemporal dynamics of the tomato fruit transcriptome under prolonged water stress
control_timing_evidence: Three drought severity levels (S1, S2, S3; from the SRA SampleName suffix) share one control arm, giving 3 control against 9 drought in every subtissue x stage cell. They are pooled into a single drought arm, so this stratum estimates the AVERAGE response across severities rather than the response at one severity. stress_level is recorded for audit but is not a blocking term: it is nested inside treatment and undefined for the controls. Checked on control-referenced log2 CPM in the leaf cell: the RFO biosynthetic arm is negative at every level (S1 -0.80, S2 -0.76, S3 -0.39) and all six testable members are negative at all three, so the pooled value is not an averaging artefact. Pooling levels inflates within-arm dispersion, which widens this stratum's standard errors rather than narrowing them.

evidence_source: BioSample attribute (treatment field) + library codes M/P x Moc/Tre; candidate publication candidate doi:10.1007/s00705-026-06532-5 (PSTVd infection enhances PEG-simulated drought stress tolerance in tomato) - not confirmed against this BioProject
control_timing_evidence: BioProject: factorial drought x PSTVd design with an untreated arm; only the mock-inoculated libraries (MMoc = well watered, MTre = drought) are used. RECORD CONFLICT: the ENA experiment title reads "RNA-seq of upland rice" while the records give Solanum lycopersicum, and the sample names do not themselves state drought. The title is read as a clerical error in a copied field. Supporting evidence from the data: this stratum shows a canonical water-deficit response - dehydrin +3.26, AREB +3.01, NCED2 +1.16, raffinose synthase +6.83, galactinol synthase +5.45, placing it among the most strongly responding strata in the cohort. That is consistent with water deficit but does not by itself exclude another ABA-inducing abiotic treatment.
